title: Seller's Property Condition Disclosure Statement
description: South Dakota Codified Laws §43-4-44 requires sellers of residential real property to provide a written property condition disclosure statement to the buyer. The disclosure must cover the seller's knowledge of the property's condition including structural, plumbing, electrical, mechanical, water, sewer, and environmental conditions. South Dakota explicitly rejects caveat emptor for residential transactions covered by this statute.

required_actions.note: Must be delivered prior to transfer. Buyer may rescind within 5 business days if disclosure reveals previously unknown defects.

metadata.note: South Dakota abandoned caveat emptor for covered residential transactions via this statute.

title: Brokerage Disclosure and Agency Relationships
description: South Dakota requires real estate licensees to provide a written disclosure of brokerage relationships to all prospective buyers and sellers at first substantive contact. Dual agency is permitted with written informed consent. Transaction brokers (facilitators) are also recognized under SDCL §36-21A.

required_actions.note: Must be delivered at first substantive contact.

title: Closing Practice — Escrow/Title Company
description: South Dakota is not an attorney-close state. Closings are typically conducted by title companies or escrow agents. Attorney involvement is optional but recommended for complex transactions. The state follows ALTA title insurance standards.

required_actions.note: Title company or escrow agent handles closing. Attorney optional.

title: Well and Septic System Disclosure
description: Sellers of properties with private wells or septic systems must disclose known conditions related to water quality, well construction, septic system age and condition. South Dakota DENR regulations require septic system inspections in certain transfer scenarios.

required_actions.note: Disclose known well and septic conditions. County may require septic inspection prior to transfer.

title: Lead-Based Paint Disclosure (Pre-1978)
description: Federal law requires disclosure of known lead-based paint hazards for residential properties built before 1978. Sellers must provide the EPA pamphlet and allow a 10-day inspection contingency.
